sections.content: How many people stayed in Coventry after gaining qualifications?

Coventry is a city in the West Midlands. Coventry also has a university.

Coventry has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Coventry ended up with:

  • a similar number of graduates as it produced
  • a similar number of non-graduates with advanced qualifications as it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 14,655 state-school pupils from Coventry who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 4,480 (31%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 4,270 (29%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Coventry to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Coventry's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Coventry in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Coventry move to?

Of Coventry's graduates, 1,070 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 100 of those graduates (9%) were living fairly locally, in the Coventry travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Coventry's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 615 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 185 of those qualified non-graduates (30%) were living fairly locally, in the Coventry travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Coventry's GCSE cohort:

  • 850 graduates left the West Midlands
  • the most common region they moved to was London
  • 330 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the West Midlands
  • the most common region they moved to was the East Midlands

In 2018 to 2019, 30% of graduates and 14% of qualified non-graduates living in Coventry had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 4,750 graduates and 4,195 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Coventry. This is compared with the 4,480 graduates and 4,270 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 70% of the graduates had also lived in Coventry as GCSE pupils, while 30% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Coventry in 2018 to 2019, 86% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 14% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
